justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish near-term outlook with gradual upward drift over time. For the 1-day estimate, I anchored closely to what appeared to be the prevailing price level around $179-180, assuming no major overnight catalyst and mean-reversion tendencies keeping the price near its recent range. For the 1-week estimate, I nudged slightly higher to $180.50, reflecting a small positive drift assumption consistent with a broad market that had been trading with moderate upward momentum. For the 1-month estimate, I moved to $182, incorporating a longer-run expectation of modest appreciation while acknowledging that over four weeks, the compounding of small daily moves could reasonably push prices higher. None of these estimates represent dramatic directional conviction — they are essentially a mild continuation of trend with minimal mean-reversion pressure assumed.

The confidence interval widths widen naturally as the horizon extends, reflecting the square-root-of-time scaling of uncertainty that characterizes most financial price processes. At one day, the $13 range ($173–$186) is relatively tight, consistent with typical daily realized volatility in this asset class. By one week, the interval expands to $25 ($168–$193), and by one month it reaches $48 ($158–$206), capturing the accumulation of daily shocks over more trading sessions. Beyond mechanical volatility scaling, I also incorporated uncertainty around macroeconomic data releases, Federal Reserve communication, and sector-specific news flows that could drive larger-than-normal single-day moves at any horizon.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals. On the downside, a surprise deterioration in macroeconomic data — particularly inflation readings coming in hotter than expected or a sharp drop in consumer confidence — could trigger a risk-off move that pushes prices well below $173 even on a one-day basis. A broader equity market sell-off driven by geopolitical escalation or a credit event could easily breach the lower bound of the one-month interval. On the upside, an unexpectedly dovish Federal Reserve signal, a strong earnings surprise, or a short-squeeze dynamic in a heavily shorted sector could accelerate gains well beyond $206 over the monthly horizon.

Finally, I want to flag that my intervals assume relatively normal market conditions with typical liquidity. In periods of elevated volatility — such as around major earnings announcements, central bank meetings, or geopolitical shocks — the actual distribution of outcomes tends to have fatter tails than a simple Gaussian model implies. This means the true probability of extreme outcomes is likely somewhat higher than my stated 90% confidence intervals suggest, and users should treat the outer bounds as soft guardrails rather than hard limits.
